results.title: What Does "Push Back" Mean for a Flight? | Otto the Agent Blog
results.content:
The best window to act is the stretch between the first delay notice and the door closing. When a schedule pushback appears on a trip booked through Otto, it checks airport-specific minimum connection times to see whether your connection still works. It searches for alternatives before it messages you, then presents options customized to your schedule for you to approve, weighing each against your next calendar commitment, cost and travel policy. Travelers finish the booking directly in the same conversation they started it, so you can choose a backup before boarding ends. [...] If the door closes first and the booking can't change, Otto keeps watching the connection and has alternatives ready when you land. With your permission, it can book a backup flight on another airline during significant delays and monitor both reservations. When the airline controls the reservation, Otto connects you with human agents at its travel partner and prepares the case first, with the trip ID, PNR, what happened and what Otto already tried.

You reach Otto in web, iOS and Android apps, and MCP-enabled experiences, plus Slack and Microsoft Teams. It's free, with no contracts, no agent-assist fees and no minimum spend, so turning it on before a tight connection costs nothing.

## Keeping the Rest of the Trip Intact [...] Start with Otto to monitor a tight connection as a departure delay develops and choose an alternative before boarding.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does "pushed back" mean the plane is leaving?

Usually it means a later departure. Aircraft pushback is the plane moving away from the gate, and it happens only after boarding ends. If you're still in the terminal with a new time posted, the plane hasn't left. If the posted time passes with no update, ask the gate agent.
